Replace the partial CIA parser with the finite strict CVSS v3 base-vector grammar. Require exactly one AV AC PR UI S C I and A metric with approved values, reject missing duplicate unknown invalid malformed and empty tokens, permit deterministic reordering, and derive only C I A into NONE LOW HIGH.

Make each AVAILABLE Technical Effect provenance-complete: preserve finding ID, CVE, exact CVSS version and vector, TechnicalEffectLevel values, non-null timezone-aware observed_at, and the unchanged existing ExplanationProvenance whose source_type is nvd and source_reference is non-empty. Missing authority cannot produce an AVAILABLE effect or READY classification.

Apply the mixed applicable-CVE fail-closed policy. Keep each CVE separate with its own vector timestamp and provenance; duplicate CVEs fail controlled. Any applicable malformed unsupported or provenance-deficient CVE makes the projection and classification readiness UNAVAILABLE with CVE-specific missing requirements. Valid other effects may remain only as explicit partial facts and can never make READY or be aggregated.

Strengthen BusinessImpactClassificationReadiness invariants so READY independently requires an AVAILABLE projection and validates every effect identity, supported version/vector grammar, NVD provenance, non-null timestamp and unique CVE. Preserve exact missing requirements and valid partial provenance for UNAVAILABLE; keep business_impact null decision null and recommendations empty.

Serialize cvss_version, original vector, finding and CVE identity, C/I/A levels, observed_at, provenance source_type and source_reference for each effect. Classification readiness must carry the same effect snapshots without lossy reconstruction.

Bind frontend effects to exactly one applicable authoritative transported TI/CVSS relationship by finding, CVE, metadata version, vector, source type/reference and observed_at. Independently re-derive C/I/A from the strict vector and then require readiness effects to equal the source-bound effect projection. Reject jointly altered copies, duplicates, missing sources, null/invalid timestamps and any identity/value/provenance mismatch.

Add the contract-specified backend adversarial tests for version mismatch, every required metric, strict values/tokens, reordered vectors, provenance/timestamp loss, classification gating, duplicate/multiple/mixed CVEs; API source transport tests; and frontend independent tampering tests plus valid single/multiple source bindings.
